{{Short description|Belgian physicist (1944–2021)}}
{{distinguish|Jean Clemens}}
'''Jean Cleymans''' (5 August 1944—22 February 2021)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Emeritus Professor Jean Cleymans: 1944–2021|url=http://www.news.uct.ac.za/article/-2021-02-22-emeritus-professor-jean-cleymans-19442021|access-date=2021-03-02|website=www.news.uct.ac.za|language=en}}</ref> was a [[Belgians|Belgian]] physicist and a professor at the [[University of Cape Town]] (UCT). He made notable contributions to the area of [[Quark–gluon plasma|quark-gluon plasma physics]] with  focus on [[Hadronization#Statistical hadronization|statistical hadronization]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last1=Redlich|first1=Krzysztof|last2=Satz|first2=Helmut|date=9 March 2021|title=Jean Willy André Cleymans (1944 – 2021)|url=https://home.cern/news/obituary/cern/jean-willy-andre-cleymans-1944-2021|access-date=2021-03-10|website=CERN|language=en}}</ref>

Jean Cleymans died in an accident in his hometown [[Turnhout]] on February 22, 2021.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|title='Verborgen parel' van de wetenschap overleden na ongelukkige val: "Nonkel Jean was inspiratiebron voor duizenden mensen"|url=https://www.nieuwsblad.be/cnt/dmf20210226_91968325|access-date=2021-03-02|website=www.nieuwsblad.be|date=26 February 2021 |language=nl-BE}}</ref>

== Education ==
Cleymans obtained his doctorate in physics in 1970 at the [[Université catholique de Louvain|University of Louvain (UCLouvain)]] in [[Louvain-la-Neuve]],<ref>{{Cite book|last=Cleymans|first=J.|url=https://bib.uclouvain.be/opac/ucl/en/chamo/chamo:557884|title=Les théories des pions mous et durs appliquées aux facteurs de forme des désintégrations faibles|date=1970|publisher=s.n.|others=UCL|location=Louvain}}{{Dead link|date=October 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Belgium and completed his post-doctoral training in 1977 with [[habilitation]] in theoretical and [[Many-body theory|particle-manybody physics]] at [[Bielefeld University]], Germany.<ref name=":2" /><ref name="M&G">''Mail & Guardian'': [http://mg.co.za/article/2015-08-28-00-professor-jean-cleynmans 'Professor Jean Cleymans'], 2015</ref>

== Work ==
Cleymans' research addressed topics pursued by the [[ALICE experiment|ALICE Collaboration]] at the [[Large Hadron Collider]] of the [[European Organization for Nuclear Research|CERN]] in Geneva, Switzerland. Together with professor Zeblon Vilakazi,<ref>{{Cite web|title=2020-06 - Top nuclear physicist to lead Wits - Wits University|url=https://www.wits.ac.za/news/latest-news/general-news/2020/2020-06/top-nuclear-physicist-to-lead-wits.html|access-date=2021-03-19|website=www.wits.ac.za}}</ref> he was instrumental in establishing the South Africa-CERN programme,<ref>{{Cite book|last=The ATLAS Collaboration|chapter=Building up the Collaboration |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/11030|title=ATLAS: A 25-Year Insider Story of the LHC Experiment|publisher=World Scientific|year=2019|isbn=978-981-327-179-1|series=Advanced Series on Directions in High Energy Physics|volume=30|page=77|language=en|doi=10.1142/9789813271807_0003|s2cid=242376159}}</ref> the successor to the UCT-CERN Research Centre.<ref name="M&G"/> He also contributed to the SA-[[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]] with Russia and was Leader of the UCT-[[ALICE Collaboration]] at CERN.<ref name="M&G"/>

Cleymans, a [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicists]], has  co-authored 299 articles and conference papers with 8,639 citations (status March 3, 2021). In addition,  he is listed on 100 LHC-ALICE experimental works which have earned more than 6,000 citations. He also edited a number of books, reports and conference proceedings. His articles have been published in a variety of international journals, among others the [[European Physical Journal]], [[Physical Review]] and [[Physics Letters]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=INSPIRE: Jean Cleymans' author profile|url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/1013367|access-date=2021-03-02|website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> Over the years he supervised 24 MSc and 17 PhD students.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="M&G" /> 

Cleymans acted as referee for several journals and was listed as a distinguished EPJ referee in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Distinguished EPJ Referees|url=https://www.epj.org/distinguished-epj-referees|access-date=2021-03-12|website=www.epj.org|publisher=EDP Sciences, Società Italiana di Fisica and Springer}}</ref> He was member of the editorial board of the [[MDPI]] journal ''Physics''<ref>{{Cite web|title=Obituary&mdash;Prof. Dr. Jean Cleymans|url=https://www.mdpi.com/about/announcements/2501|access-date=2021-03-12|website=MDPI}}</ref> and he served as chairman of the South Africa-CERN Programme.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Swingler|first=Helen|date=25 October 2013|title=Nobel a smashing cause for celebration|url=http://www.news.uct.ac.za/article/-2013-10-25-nobel-a-smashing-cause-for-celebration|access-date=2021-03-12|website=www.news.uct.ac.za|language=en}}</ref>

== Family ==
Cleymans was married to Ria (Maria) since 1968, they have two daughters Sylvie (1969-2021) and Silke (1980).{{cn|date=March 2021}}

== Awards ==
* Elected Fellow of the [[Royal Society of South Africa]] (1993)<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Academy of Europe: Cleymans Jean|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Cleymans_Jean|access-date=2021-03-11|website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref>
*[[Alexander von Humboldt Research Award]] (1999)
* Prize of the Polish Ministry of National Education for Research Excellence (2000)
* Prize of the Polish Ministry of National Education for Outstanding Team Research (2003)<ref name="M&G"/>
